# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile canvas sniper/stealth shooter with two preserved modes: scoped target identification and close-range ghost run.
- objective: identify the uniquely described target in a moving crowd, fire accurately, then win immediately in sniper mode or escape after the hit in ghost mode.
- input model: one-thumb friendly drag on playfield to move scope/camera or virtual joystick, plus a large FIRE button.
- core loop: start session, generate cyber city/crowd, read target colors, track target, shoot, handle hit/miss/wrong target, resolve win/loss/retry.
- fail/friction state: wrong target or miss triggers panic; ghost mode also uses ammo, cover signal, cameras, guard attack, and exit reachability.

## Protected mechanics
- Drag-to-aim scope behavior and tap FIRE action are preserved.
- Hit detection remains based on scope/camera coordinates against NPC body bounds.
- Target descriptors remain color-based and tied to generated NPC attributes.
- Wrong target, miss, panic, ammo drain, cover signal, ghost cloak, guard aggression, win/loss, retry/menu states are preserved.

## Remixed target
Sniper Game. A satirical game inspired by Spider-Verse built around sniper game play, with competitive, futuristic, leaderboard energy, after work session design, search-friendly hooks like sniper game, shooter, fps, aesthetics like chrome aesthetic, cyberpunk, neon aesthetic, and meme-tone cues such as no scope, main character. Designed for one-thumb mobile play with touch-friendly interactions, responsive readability, fast onboarding, and portrait-first UX tuned for iOS and Android in the 4:7 to 9:16 range. The rebuilt public surface frames the same mechanics as No-Scope Mainframe: a chrome cyberpunk after-work leaderboard contract where a main-character sharpshooter deplatforms an Algorithm CEO in a comic-prism city.
